ledger.claim: The artifacts that carry the billing and route facts are all the same trip: the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown each bear trip_id TRP-00712, and their timestamps agree — the trace runs 09:18:40 to 09:42:40, matching the trip record's started_at 09:18:40 and ended_at 09:42:40, with the fare breakdown charged at 09:43:00. The rider's threshold burden of showing the artifacts describe one and the same trip under POL-RD-08 is therefore met on the face of the record, and the dispute is ripe for decision on the merits.

On this trip's own trace there is no distance deviation: trace_distance_km is 11.99 against an optimal_distance_km of 12.2, an excess of -0.21 km, or -1.72%, which fails both limbs of POL-RD-01 (the excess must exceed 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms). The rider does not argue otherwise and does not seek a distance refund. That does not dispose of the dispute, because POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-09(4) make a billing-integrity correction available whether or not any deviation exists, and it is that limb this case runs on.

The fare breakdown charges three ERP lines totalling SGD 14.00, but the trace crosses only two of them. West link entry (SGD 3.00) and Canal link exit (SGD 3.00) each have a nearest fix at 0.0 m — fixes at index 40 and index 104 sit on the gantry coordinates. The third line, North service-loop ERP at SGD 8.00, is carried as crossed: false, with the trace's closest approach 16,784.57 m away — more than sixty times the 250 m gantry match radius POL-RD-09(4) prescribes. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is 28.00 — so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider. POL-RD-11(a) fixes her remedy as charged_total 42.00 less quoted_fare 28.00 less the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 (ERP actually crossed 6.00, airport surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00) = SGD 8.00; the fare ledger itself publishes that same figure as pol_rd_11_remedy. Against the SGD 14.00 ERP charge the rider contests, that is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.00.

The SGD 8.00 is one sum, not two. The phantom North service-loop line (SGD 8.00) and the excess of charged_total over quoted_fare plus properly chargeable lines (also SGD 8.00) are the same money seen from the two ends of one arithmetic; POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding the pass-through correction on top of the POL-RD-11(a) figure, since the off-route line is already excluded from adequately chargeable lines. The rider asks for SGD 8.00 once, itemised rather than double-counted.

The driver's own words do not enlarge what was chargeable on this trip. His chat message asserts 'ERP fourteen total. Air pollution fee sixty extra' — a SGD 60 pollution fee that appears on no line of the fare ledger — and his counterparty statement concedes only that he 'mentioned extra costs' while confirming 'the app invoice carries the ERP entries'. The rider replied that she would pay only the app invoice. POL-RD-11 ties the rider's exposure to the pass-through and statutory lines the fare_breakdown actually carries, and a SGD 60 charge that no artifact records is not one of them; the driver's characterisation of what was chargeable is not a reliable guide to what the ledger properly carries.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory at all. EV-ADVIS-00712-01 is MISSING — weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window' — and its absence is itself citable. Under POL-RD-13 no external traffic cause can be run against this trip: POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record, so no closure, queue or incident can adjust the optimal baseline or re-characterise the ERP lines the ledger actually charged. This claim relies on an artifact the admissibility pre-pass returned as MISSING at weight 0.0, and the impairment is disclosed here rather than presented as clean.

No route deviation is established on this trip, so the premise of a distance-based dispute fails at the outset. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement, and it is 11.99 km against an optimal_distance_km of 12.2 km - an excess of -0.21 km, or -1.72%. Both establishment tests fail: the excess is neither more than 20% of the optimal distance nor more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. No deviation exists and no distance refund is available however the rider characterises the trip; trip_record.actual_distance_km (12.0 km) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with a quoted_fare_sgd of 28.00, so POL-RD-02's distance-and-time recomputation does not run and POL-RD-11 governs instead. The distance and time charges were fixed at booking and a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines; no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large any excess might be. The rider's remedy is confined to the pass-through and statutory lines dealt with in POL-RD-11(a) and (b).

The two ERP lines the vehicle actually crossed - West link entry and Canal link exit, SGD 3.00 each - are properly chargeable pass-throughs under POL-RD-09 and are not refundable to the rider. Each line is on the optimal route and the driver's trace passes within 0.0 m of it, so both are metered ERPs actually crossed on this trip. The SGD 6.00 they represent stands.

The rider's pooled-itinerary theory fails at the first step. trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_XL, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and the booked optimal of 12.2 km is the correct comparator - against which, as above, the trace is short rather than long. A chat reference to pooling by the driver does not convert a solo XL trip into a platform-matched pooled itinerary, and the rider's invocation of the pooled baseline has cited nothing.

No pollution or green fee was ever billed on this trip. The fare breakdown carries base fare, distance fare, time fare, platform fee and ERP lines only, and contains no air-pollution line at all; the SGD 60 the driver mentioned in chat was a stated potential extra cost, not a ledger entry, and the rider was billed nothing for it. Nothing in the contested SGD 14.00 turns on any pollution charge.

Concession, and it fixes the ceiling on this dispute: the only charge line that is not properly chargeable is the North service-loop ERP of SGD 8.00, whose nearest trace fix is 16,784.57 m away, so the line was never crossed and cannot be a charge for a gantry actually crossed. That single line is a billing-integrity correction refundable under POL-RD-09(4) and POL-RD-11(a) - charged_total 42.00 less quoted_fare 28.00 less properly chargeable pass-throughs 6.00 leaves 8.00 - so at most SGD 8.00 is refundable, not the SGD 14.00 the rider seeks, and no larger sum is available on an upfront-quoted trip.

If POL-RD-06 were consulted, its pattern test fails on the driver's side. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 250, so the trailing-90-day count is below the threshold of 3 and the ratio is below 0.05; no repeat-deviation pattern is established and neither the POL-RD-06(b) uplift nor the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows. Those two fields are the only profile fields this test names - the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is not the field the clause asks for.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties are addressed. Rider: your dispute is partly upheld. This was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_breakdown.fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 28.00) and it was charged a total of SGD 42.00. Distance and time were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available — and in any event nothing turns on distance here: the governing trace figure is 11.99 km against an optimal 12.2 km, an excess of -0.21 km (-1.72%), which fails both limbs of POL-RD-01. What does move is the ERP pass-through. Three ERP lines totalling SGD 14.00 were charged. Two were genuinely crossed: West link entry (SGD 3.00) and Canal link exit (SGD 3.00), each with a trace fix sitting at 0.0 m. The third, 'North service-loop ERP' (SGD 8.00), was charged although the trace's closest approach is 16,784.57 m — over sixty times the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09(4) uses. A charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full. Under POL-RD-11(a) the sum is: charged total 42.00 less quoted fare 28.00 less properly chargeable pass-throughs 6.00 (the two crossed ERP lines; airport surcharge 0.00, waiting-time fee 0.00) = SGD 8.00, and the fare ledger publishes that same figure as pol_rd_11_remedy (8.00). That is the amount refunded. It is one sum, not two: the phantom line and the excess of the charged total over quote plus chargeable lines are the same money, and POL-RD-09(1) forbids counting it twice. Driver: your claims are answered. It is accepted that no route deviation is established (excess -0.21 km on the trace, which governs over the rounded trip_record figure of 12.0 km), that this is an upfront-quoted trip, that the two crossed ERP lines are properly chargeable, that no pollution or green fee was ever billed (no such line exists on the ledger), and that driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips so no POL-RD-06 pattern, uplift or conduct referral arises. Your mention of 'ERP fourteen total. Air pollution fee sixty extra' in the chat log is noted, but a SGD 60 pollution fee appears on no ledger line and nothing was billed for it, so it does not change what was chargeable; POL-RD-11 ties the rider's exposure to the lines the fare_breakdown actually carries. The rider's pooling theory also fails: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_XL, not RYDE_POOL, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply. On the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00712-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT): no party asserted an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-03 is unavailable on the record and nothing adjusts the optimal baseline — this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and the phantom line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4) rather than escalating under POL-RD-10(8). The artifacts that carry the deciding facts — the fare ledger and the GPS trace — are both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is capped at 1.0; nothing below weight 1.0 carries any deciding fact. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation. The billing-integrity finding is referred as required.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 8.00 'North service-loop ERP' line was charged for a gantry the GPS trace never crossed (closest approach 16,784.57 m against the 250 m match radius). Record the phantom-line charge as a billing-integrity finding and review the gantry matching for trip TRP-00712.
